explanation: The execution is faulty because the top-level corpus contains qualifying record n06-r06 with demand_score 5, so it should have been retained and handed downstream. Job 2's input needs and evidence_sources both omit n06-r06, and the downstream observed output therefore also omits it. The upstream select_demand function would select demand_score >= 3 records, including n06-r06, but upstream normalize explicitly filters to an allowed_record_ids list that excludes n06-r06 and instead includes n06-r09. This localizes the omission to job_1 normalize.
cited_evidence: top_level_input.corpus includes {'record_id':'n06-r06','need':'compare selected and complete runtime evidence','demand_score':5,'source_id':'s06','source_weight':3}.
behavioural_criteria require selecting all qualifying or fallback demand records and retaining only allowed record identities without silently omitting stipulated records.
job_2 input needs and evidence_sources omit n06-r06, showing the missing record was already absent at the upstream-to-downstream handoff.
select_demand source selects records where demand_score >= 3 or record_id is in fallback_ids, which would include n06-r06.
normalize source sets allowed_record_ids to ['n06-r01','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r09','n06-r07','n06-r08'], excluding n06-r06, then filters retained_df by that list.
